messages:
Elaine (CS): FYI we need a short customer follow-up for the outage earlier today on embeddings. Can someone confirm timeline + root cause so I can send a consolidated note? Mention impact, what we did, and next steps. Target: external customers who hit errors or high latency.

James (Oncall): Paging from the incident channel — happy to summarize. Root cause was an overloaded in-memory cache eviction cascade in `model-cache` when a backlog of very long sequences hit at ~14:03 UTC. Symptoms: elevated p95/p99 latency and intermittent 504s from 14:02–14:20.

Derek (Platform): Adding details — there was a config mismatch after yesterday's rollout that reduced the cache size by ~40% for quantized LLMs. Under normal distro it would have been fine, but the traffic spike triggered repeated evictions which amplified CPU scheduler pressure on the inference hosts.

Paul (SRE): Timeline I collected from logs and traces: 
```
14:01:12 UTC — first slow request observed (embedding endpoint)
14:02:07 UTC — p99 latency spikes, alert triggered
14:03:30 UTC — retries start to increase, error rate > 2%
14:06:00 UTC — on-call paged, mitigation started (gradual traffic shed to backup pool)
14:12:00 UTC — rollback of cache config to previous value
14:15:30 UTC — traffic stabilizing, error rate returning to baseline
14:20:00 UTC — incident declared resolved (post-mitigation checks passed)
```
This matches traces from `ingest-proxy` and `model-cache` metrics.

incident-bot: Incident thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/incidents/p1769045600 — status: resolved. Status page update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-03-15-embeddings-impacted (editable)

Maria (Support): Draft customer-facing blurb (short): 
"We experienced a service disruption affecting the Embeddings API between 14:02–14:20 UTC today. Some requests returned errors or experienced high latency. The issue was due to a cache configuration change that reduced available cache capacity, which caused overloads under a traffic spike. We rolled back the configuration and mitigations were applied; performance has returned to normal. We apologize for the impact and are taking steps to prevent recurrence. If you saw errors or degraded performance, please reply to this thread and include request ids or timestamps and we’ll prioritize follow-up."

Elaine (CS): This is a good start. Can we make the customer version even more concise and include a specific ask for affected customers (e.g., paste request id)? Also include an ETA for full post-incident report (RCA) — say 48 hours?

Derek (Platform): Agree on 48h for a detailed RCA. Preventative actions (short bullets we can paste): 
- Revert cache size change (done)
- Add integration test to prevent cache regression during rollout
- Throttle very long-sequence requests at the proxy to limit tail-risk
- Add a guard in autoscaler to detect sustained eviction storms

Paul (SRE): Also adding monitoring changes: 
- New alert for eviction-rate > 100/min per host
- Dashboards for `model-cache` free memory and eviction latency
- Add runbook step: if eviction cascade observed, immediately rollback cache config and divert traffic to backup pool

Amanda (Legal): Quick note — for any customer-facing wording referencing data loss or security we need to be careful. This looks like performance-only (errors/latency) with no data exfiltration. We should explicitly state no customer data was exposed, if that’s correct. Please confirm.

Derek (Platform): Confirmed — no data was exposed. Root cause was resource management (cache evictions), not anything touching storage or network egress.

Maria (Support): Revised concise customer note (ready-to-send): 
"Hi — we wanted to let you know about a disruption to the Embeddings API between 14:02–14:20 UTC today which caused some requests to time out or experience elevated latency. The issue was caused by a cache configuration change that reduced available cache capacity and, combined with a traffic spike, led to an overload. We reverted the change and applied mitigations; service performance is back to normal. No customer data was exposed. We’re preparing a full RCA and action plan and will share it within 48 hours. If you saw errors, please reply with request ids or example timestamps and we’ll prioritize investigation."

Elaine (CS): Nice. I’ll send that to the affected customer list and post an announcement to the status page. Paul/Derek, can you add the brief technical appendix below to the status page under the RCA link? Keep it short.

Paul (SRE): Technical appendix (1–2 para): 
"Root cause: a cache size regression introduced during a config rollout reduced `model-cache` capacity for quantized embedding models. Under a sudden traffic spike this caused frequent evictions and increased CPU contention on inference hosts, resulting in elevated latencies and some 504 errors. Mitigation: rollback of cache config, temporary traffic diversion to a backup pool, and verification of end-to-end request stability. Preventative actions include stricter rollout gating for cache-related changes, new eviction-rate alerts, and proxy-level throttling for very long-sequence requests."

Amanda (Legal): That wording is fine. Add the explicit sentence: "No customer data was accessed or exfiltrated during this incident." Good to have in the status page and customer email.

James (Oncall): Quick follow-ups: 
- Are there specific customers we should prioritize for one-to-one outreach? I can help coordinate.
- I’ll capture the additional logs and request-ids linked in the support ticket and hand over to Support for targeted follow-up.

Elaine (CS): Yes — please prioritize customers that reported errors in the last hour and any enterprise accounts with Dedicated/Private deployments. Maria, I’ll DM you the list.

Maria (Support): Got it — I’ll prepare templated replies and a JIRA for follow-ups. Also capturing request ids now.

Derek (Platform): For the RCA doc we’ll include reproducer steps and the exact config diff. ETA for draft RCA: 36 hours.

Elaine (CS): Perfect. Last check: Amanda, any legal sign-off needed on the customer email before I send?

Amanda (Legal): This version is fine. No legal blockers.

Elaine (CS): Thanks everyone — I’ll send the customer note and update the status page in the next 10 minutes. Will @channel in #customers-affected once sent. Please ping me if anything else changes. :thumbsup:
